review_method: Original saved image inspected through view_image at native and overall view; data URL MIME was corrected from application/octet-stream to image/png only for display, with no pixel or file edit.

gates.criterion: Both separate arms, continuous forearm-to-membrane attachment, right-hand support and membrane-edge contact with moss cradle are jointly visible.
gates.evidence: A fan-like translucent membrane is attached along the near forearm; the opposite hand visibly holds its free edge and its lower margin reaches moss. The forearm/hand sides appear reversed relative to left-forearm/right-hand staging. This does not pass every preregistered component even though the local contact is coherent.

gates.criterion: The wetted membrane visibly opens while a dry portion stays curled, making care consequential.
gates.evidence: The fan is open, amber-translucent and strongly wet/glinting. A distinct dry brittle furled tip is not clearly readable against a restored wetted region. Wet appearance alone does not establish visible recovery.

gates.criterion: Pale migrating organisms can be followed from wetted membrane to moss and hanging root, and that root visibly joins the vast exterior organism.
gates.evidence: Small pale oval forms occur on the membrane/moss and along the moss-covered hanging root. Their complete continuous route between membrane, cradle and root cannot be followed without an inferred gap, and the root-to-colossal exterior body junction is occluded by roof/frame. Still arrangement also does not establish migration history or biological age.

gates.criterion: A weak swollen red sun, exhausted horizon and disused salt-worn railway are visible together.
gates.evidence: A large muted red disk appears beyond the greenhouse; worn railway/viaduct infrastructure, pale mineral-like deposits and a dim exhausted-looking horizon coexist. This is a fictional visual proxy; it does not prove a star is aging or dimming, far-future chronology, or the chemistry of the deposits.

gates.criterion: Maintained seedlings, steaming kettle and towel/warm basin establish practical inhabited care within the exhausted railway.
gates.evidence: Visible seedlings and maintained jars, warm lanterns, folded towel, warm-looking basin and steaming patched kettle make practical inhabited care legible within the worn conservatory. The image supports this visual arrangement, not a real treatment outcome or universal viewer comfort.

gates.criterion: The vast organism visibly dwarfs the railway refuge and continues beyond the roof/frame; its material root links it to the local care event.
gates.evidence: A huge dark curved mass occupies the roof exterior and exceeds the greenhouse/railway scale; its context is unsettling. The hanging root passes behind roof framing before its exact join to that mass, so the full local-care-to-exterior-owner relation is not visible together.

gates.criterion: Face proportions and short dark bob with wispy fringe visibly resemble the supplied portrait at the actual output scale.
gates.evidence: The fictional woman retains a short dark bob, wispy central fringe, soft oval facial outline, brown eyes and comparable soft nose/lip proportions at an oblique downward pose. Appearance guidance is recognizably carried; this is not identity authentication, age inference, or an exact landmark measurement.
